title: Chronos probe scheduler and SLO-aware eviction
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: Our existing readiness/liveness probe fabric floods control plane and autoscaler signals during staggered cold starts and regional failover, causing thrash and missed SLO windows. Current probes are statically scheduled and do not account for warmed KV caches, token-priority traffic, or circuit-breaker state, which leads to noisy health signals during high load and multi-region failover events.

Goal: Implement a new 'Chronos' probe scheduler and an SLO-aware eviction policy for probe-driven instance health so that: (1) probe noise is reduced by 60% during warmup/failover, (2) autoscaler stability (measured by scaling flaps per hour) improves 40%, and (3) SLO violations tied to probe-induced shedding drop to near-zero in canary environments.

Scope: Chronos scheduler (adaptive sampling + backoff), probe credits & token-aware prioritization, KV-cache-aware probe dampening, probe-shadowing for canaries, and an SLO-aware eviction leash that integrates with autoscaler cooldown and circuit-breakers. This ticket covers design, implementation of an operator in the runtime, integration tests, and a staged rollout and monitoring plan.

Out-of-scope: Changes to external load balancers, customer-facing API schema, or global rollout until canaries are validated.
acceptance_criteria: Chronos scheduler implements adaptive probe intervals based on per-instance warmness and recent probe success history
Probe credit system limits probe fanout per region and enforces backpressure during autoscaler cooldown windows
KV-cache-aware dampening suppresses readiness probes for endpoints with >80% cache hit rate unless explicit failure observed
SLO-aware eviction policy refrains from evicting nodes during transient probe storms; eviction requires sustained degraded score beyond configured leash
Automated integration test simulates multi-region failover and demonstrates reduced autoscaler thrash and preserved request-level SLOs in the canary cluster
Dashboards and alerts (dash URL in links) are published showing probe rate, probe failures, eviction decisions, autoscale events, and SLO impact

notes: Design rationale: Static probes were designed for simplicity but do not reflect runtime state (KV cache, in-flight tokens). Chronos treats probes as a scarce resource and schedules them like a rate-limited heartbeat to minimize control-plane amplification.

Key idea: Maintain a per-instance 'warmness' score (0-1) derived from KV cache hit ratio, recent successful inference latency, and recent probe success. Probe interval = base_interval * f(warmness, recent_failures) with exponential backoff on failures and soft-recovery on success.

Probe credit model: Regions get a credit bucket (tokens) replenished at a configurable rate. Each probe consumption depends on request weight (e.g., long-context or priority tokens cost more). This prevents a mass of low-impact probes from causing an autoscaler reaction.

SLO-aware eviction leash: Eviction decisions consult the leash window. If multiple readiness failures are detected within short windows but autoscaler cooldown active, the eviction is delayed until either (a) sustained failure threshold exceeded, or (b) manual override. This reduces harmful thrash during failover.
Circuit-breaker integration: When a circuit is open for a route, Chronos reduces probe intensity for nodes serving that route to avoid generating misleading unhealthy signals.

Canary strategy: Enable 'probe-shadow' flag in canary cluster to run logical probes without incrementing regional credits; observe behavior for 72 hours before incrementally enabling credit accounting.

Metrics to add: chronos_probe_interval_seconds, chronos_probe_credits_remaining, chronos_warmness_score, chronos_eviction_leash_count, chronos_probe_shadow_count, autoscaler_flap_rate, slo_request_p95_latency_over_time

Non-goal: This ticket does not modify primary autoscaler control-loop algorithm; it supplies stabilized health signals and eviction recommendations. Autoscaler will still make final scaling decisions unless we merge later as a separate work item.

runbook: Initial runbook actions: (1) If probe-induced eviction is suspected, toggle chronos.eviction_leash=on to hold evictions; (2) Enable probe-shadow on canary cluster if false positives observed; (3) If autoscaler flaps persist, reduce probe replenishment rate for the region and escalate to SRE oncall.
risks: Mistuning credit rates could starve real health checks and delay detection of actual failures. Overly aggressive dampening of probes could mask genuine node regressions. We'll mitigate with canary-shadowing and automatic rollback triggers based on SLO regressions.
